name: Terminal History Index & Diagnostics Efficiency
changes: Adds a no-op terminal-history sync fast path so the 2-second completion monitor does not copy, sort, or rebuild the full durable history when no terminal row changed.
Makes a durable terminal-history mutation own exactly one index rebuild; removals no longer rebuild once before the write and again inside the write.
Adds terminal-history sync/no-op/rebuild-avoidance telemetry so full-load diagnostics can prove that unchanged passes stay cheap as history grows toward 5,000 rows.
Makes /api/diagnostics consume the scope-native Live snapshot and report operational tracked/presentable jobs separately from durable Completed/Failed/Cancelled history counts.
Reports unmeasured provider latency/success as N/A instead of 0 ms / None%, while preserving raw runtime connection state from the private SAB engine.
Retains current and last multi-active overlap signatures and identifies raw SAB overlap versus visible-card normalization without changing the one-foreground-package presentation rule.

Preserves private SABnzbd 5.1.2 transfer/repair/extraction authority plus all v3.6.54 compaction, v3.6.53 identity-gate, Smart Import, Library Integrity, Selected Episodes and runtime-handoff protections.
regression_guards: Repeated unchanged terminal-history syncs must not increase terminal-history index rebuild or write counters.
One actual terminal-history mutation must produce one durable write and one index rebuild while preserving Completed/Failed counts and page-native history behavior.
Removing a durable history row must rebuild exactly once and keep the retained history/index consistent.
Diagnostics must use scope-native Live Downloads, expose durable terminal counts separately from operational tracked counts, and must not print 0 ms / None% for unmeasured providers.
Multi-active telemetry must retain the last overlap signature and expose whether the current overlap comes from raw SAB state, visible-card normalization, or both.
All v3.6.54 compaction/startup, v3.6.53 NZB identity, SAB 5.1.2, Library Integrity, Selected Episodes and earlier production guards remain mandatory.
